name: Metallurgy
boundaries: Metallurgy: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: The revised concept requires calibrated, prospective prediction across several unseen families, rather than exact design of any desired property.

original_dispositions.original_title: Intrinsic autonomous self-healing in crystalline structural metals
original_dispositions.reason: Autonomous healing remains central; assisted composite work is identified separately as related evidence.

original_dispositions.original_title: Infinite fatigue life under any cyclic loading
original_dispositions.reason: A universal guarantee under arbitrary loading and environments is not a physically useful completion target. A bounded, robust fatigue-suppression capability could be revolutionary, but the historical item does not specify a distinct demonstrated principle or sufficiently concrete capability beyond the damage-management goal in MET-04. MET-04 does not claim to achieve fatigue immunity.

original_dispositions.original_title: Defect-free bulk metallic glasses in arbitrary sizes and compositions
original_dispositions.reason: Narrowed to manufacturable, damage-tolerant parts in practical compositions.

original_dispositions.original_title: Room-temperature superplasticity in low-cost ferrous and aluminum alloys
original_dispositions.reason: Limited room-temperature superplasticity in a laboratory Al–Zn alloy has already been demonstrated; industrial forming remains the proposed breakthrough.

original_dispositions.original_title: Absolute immunity to all forms of corrosion
original_dispositions.reason: Added in narrowed form, with specified environments and multiple damage modes replacing the universal-immunity claim.

original_dispositions.original_title: Uncoated alloys stable above 1,600 °C in oxidizing atmospheres
original_dispositions.reason: System-level efficiency and flight claims remain conditional.

original_dispositions.original_title: Perfect industrial single-crystal growth for any alloy
original_dispositions.reason: Single-crystal superalloy turbine blades are already manufactured, and the historical entry does not establish why zero defects in every alloy is necessary for a field-changing capability. Better prediction of processing and defects overlaps MET-01. Experiments on CMSX-4 found freckles under one solidification direction and freckle-free castings under another; this is process-specific, not universal perfection.

original_dispositions.original_title: Property-preserving infinite recyclability of all engineering alloys
original_dispositions.reason: Partly covered for steel and aluminum respectively. The universal claim across all alloys and unlimited cycles is not demonstrated; titanium and other alloy families are not thereby covered.

original_dispositions.original_title: Ductile, lightweight intermetallics or quasicrystals with ceramic-level hardness
original_dispositions.reason: The proposed combination could be consequential, but the entry provides no substantiated material mechanism or defined application in which the simultaneous historical numerical targets would be necessary. As written, it is a desired bundle of properties rather than a sufficiently specified distinct breakthrough. MET-01 could help search for such materials, but does not itself deliver them.

reconciliation_change_log.change: MET-01 through MET-06 are retained with their original identities. MET-02 now includes the HYBRIT pilot alongside the molten-oxide-electrolysis milestone. MET-04 now cites the accessible full paper and distinguishes autonomous nanoscale healing from assisted composite repair.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The HYBRIT addition makes the route-neutral scope clearer.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Added MET-07 for manufacturable, damage-tolerant bulk metallic glasses; MET-08 for practical room-temperature superplastic forming; MET-09 for uncoated high-temperature structural alloys; MET-10 for high-value mixed-aluminum recycling; and MET-11 for broadly reliable intrinsic corrosion resistance.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Each defines an application-scale capability rather than retaining unsupported universality or numerical impact claims.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Corrected the historical citation of Ian Baker’s “Grand Challenges in Metals and Alloys”: it appeared in Frontiers in Metals and Alloys, not Materials Today, on 3 May 2022, DOI: 10.3389/ftmal.2022.894403.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Its “Materials Problems” section discusses broad challenges, but does not establish the historical list as a canonical set of ten.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Corrected the historical journal attribution for Sarbajit Banerjee, Y. Shirley Meng, Andrew M. Minor and colleagues, “Materials laboratories of the future for alloys, amorphous, and composite materials”: it is an MRS Bulletin article, 2025, DOI: 10.1557/s43577-024-00846-y, not a Nature Reviews Materials article.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Its opening discusses integrating prediction, processing, characterization and manufacturing; it does not demonstrate a universal alloy engine.
